reason: At base the JIT fastpath assigns the swallowed-issue value, so safeParse({}) returns data with key a present ("leaked"), violating the expected absence of the key; the PR exists precisely to fix this.

At head the generated branch guards both the issue concat and the value assignment on !issues.length || present, so an absent optional key with a swallowed issue yields no key, and a present failing key still fails, matching the test.
At base the paragraph continuation lookahead only treats space-only lines as blank, so the tab-only line is absorbed as a lazy continuation and only one paragraph is produced, not two.
At head the widened [ \t]+\n lookahead makes a tab-only line a blank separator, so the parser emits two distinct paragraphs as expected.
The PR only touches error-path stack decoration in the catch handler; successful JSON responses are parsed by the default transformResponse at both revisions, so data is a parsed object.
The change affects only error stack decoration and leaves response parsing untouched, so a successful application/json response still resolves with data as a parsed object at head.
A plain boolean flag like --verbose is handled by the normal option parser at both revisions; the PR only changes negative-number argument detection, which is unrelated to this behaviour.
The regex change only affects negative-number argument detection; a plain boolean flag like --verbose is recognized by the normal option parsing at both revisions.
At base JsonTreeReader.nextInt goes straight to JsonPrimitive.getAsInt, and Integer.parseInt silently coerces full-width Unicode digits to 123, so no parsing error is raised as the test expects.
At head nextInt validates the string token with validateAscii and throws MalformedJsonException for full-width digits, matching the expected clear parsing error.
At base parseSearchPath uses the alphanumeric-only regex, so 'test-db' is split into 'test' and 'db' and the issued SQL sets two schemas instead of the single quoted name.
At head the blocklist regex [^\s,"\']+ keeps 'test-db' as one token, so the connector issues set search_path to the single schema "test-db" as expected.

The PR only changes ByteBufferUtil stream-reading buffer recycling, which is unrelated to request option handling; transformations remain applied by default when loading into an ImageView at both revisions.
The ByteBufferUtil buffer-recycling fix does not touch request option handling, so a center-crop transformation is still applied by default at head when not explicitly disabled.

At base allowedSymbolsAndAlphanumerics is recomputed as the union of configured symbols and alphanumerics on every check, so an identifier using a configured allowed symbol produces no violation; the PR is only a caching optimization.

The cached set is refreshed via didSet when allowed_symbols is applied and the PR reports identical violation output, so identifiers with configured allowed symbols still pass the naming rule at head.
The GCC 15 header fix is unrelated to image loading; node-canvas at this revision does not percent-decode non-base64 data URI payloads, so the SVG fails to load like the known issue describes.

The Afrikaans locale PR does not touch shift arithmetic; arrow's shift adds wall-clock hours via timedelta, yielding 04:30-05:00 across the spring-forward boundary rather than the expected 05:30-05:00 from absolute elapsed time.
The cstdint include only fixes compilation on GCC 15 and leaves data URI handling unchanged, so the percent-encoded SVG data URI still fails to decode and load at head.
The cookie-parsing PR is unrelated to body decoding; Vapor's urlencoded-form decoder at this revision throws on an empty body, so the all-optional type decode returns 422 instead of succeeding.

Parsing directives from all Cookie headers does not change content decoding, so an empty application/x-www-form-urlencoded body still fails to decode into the all-optional type at head, returning 422.

The PR only fixes spelling in tests and comments; MemMapFs.Remove at this revision does not reject a non-empty directory, so no error is returned and the removal behaviour diverges from a real filesystem.
The spelling-only PR leaves MemMapFs.Remove unchanged, so removing the non-empty /dirname still succeeds without the expected not-empty error at head.

The PR only fixes a json_encode call in a test and does not touch the Comparator; when one removed index matches two added indexes the diff logic still raises the undefined array key PHP warning at base.
The JSON flags test fix is unrelated to schema comparison, so the ambiguous two-candidate index rename still triggers the PHP undefined-array-key warning at head.

The Afrikaans locale strings do not affect shift semantics; arrow performs wall-clock timedelta addition at base, producing 04:30-05:00 instead of the expected 05:30-05:00 across the spring-forward transition.

The CircuitBreaker predicate-leak fix does not touch the semaphore rate limiter; lowering limitForPeriod below available permits still stops the scheduled refresh task from replenishing, so admissions halt at base.

The PR only changes CircuitBreakerStateMachine predicate handling, leaving the rate limiter's changeLimitForPeriod refresh bug intact at head, so permits are never replenished after the limit is lowered.

ESLint's no-var autofix refuses to rewrite a var whose references appear before the declaration in source order, so the file is left unchanged and still prints undefined via var hoisting; the prefer-template PR is unrelated.

The reference to count lies textually after var count so no-var rewrites it to let/const, and invoking printCount before the declaration then hits the temporal dead zone and throws instead of printing undefined.

The log-formatter fix is unrelated; JOBDIR persists the pending request queue and seen list, so restarting the SitemapSpider resumes crawling the queued sitemap URLs rather than closing after zero pages.
The logformatter_adapter change only affects log argument formatting; the persisted JOBDIR queue still replays pending sitemap requests at head, so the resumed crawl continues past zero pages.

The sanitize PR does not touch wrapping or highlight rendering; printing a double-width character with a full-row highlight at terminal-width 1 still triggers bat's known capacity-overflow panic at base.
The bidi sanitize fix is unrelated to row-background painting; with width-2 characters in a 1-column terminal the theme's full-row background fill still underflows and aborts at head.

The syslog regexp optimization is unrelated to the file output plugin; when one batch contains multiple chunk keys, the known symlink_path behaviour creates the symlink for only one key, not both aa and bb.
The RFC5424 parsing change does not affect symlink handling; the key whose symlink was skipped by the earlier multi-key batch remains without an up-to-date symlink at head.
The ConcurrentBag virtual-thread change is unrelated; pool construction at base still goes through System properties access whose global lock can be held by unrelated code, so creation can block.
The ConcurrentBag virtual-thread spin change does not touch pool-name generation or system property access, so concurrent pool creation can still contend on the shared Properties lock at head.
The SORT ACL fix is unrelated to persistence; on 32-bit builds the background save of a multi-megabyte dataset still fails (terminated by signal rather than success) at base.
ACL key parsing for SORT does not affect the RDB child process; the 32-bit server's background save still terminates by signal instead of saving successfully at head.
The CWD fix is unrelated; do_addsub only supports decimal numbers up to its internal digit cap, so the 47-digit number exceeds it and CTRL-A does not produce the exact increment at base.
The nvim_win_set_buf CWD change does not touch number incrementing; CTRL-X on the 47-digit number still exceeds the supported length and fails to decrement exactly at head.
The file-cache race fix does not affect operator type resolution; concatenating an array with untyped NULL still collapses the result to a scalar INTEGER NULL instead of an array-typed NULL at base.

The external file cache fix does not change type resolution of || versus list_concat, so the pipe operator still reports the collapsed scalar INTEGER type at head while list_concat reports the array type.

The ScrollBar touchscreen fix is unrelated; at base the PREDELETE notification for a released RefCounted is delivered too late in destruction, so reading members crashes or the object is already invalid.
The input-handling change does not alter RefCounted destruction ordering, so the NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE handler still runs on a partially destroyed object and crashes at head.

The tree criterion change is unrelated; f_regression at base still divides by the zero variance of a constant column, producing NaN scores and the invalid-value warning instead of a finite 0.0 F-score.

The categorical absolute_error guard does not touch feature_selection; for a near-constant column r_regression still takes sqrt of a numerically negative value at head, emitting the RuntimeWarning and NaN.
The swagger UI fix is unrelated to the agent process; at base the file sink does not apply the configured octal mode, so the token file is not created with 640 permissions.
The swagger UI change is unrelated to the agent's sink writing; the configured 0600 octal mode is still not applied to the token file at head, so permissions are not restricted to the owner.
At base write_usage with empty args emits only a blank line because wrap_text discards the usage prefix, so the first line of --help is not 'Usage: cli' (issue #3360).
At head write_usage writes the stripped usage prefix followed by a newline when args is empty, so a command with no options or arguments renders exactly 'Usage: cli'.
Returning a dict from a Flask view has long been converted to a compact JSON response with application/json Content-Type; the IPv6 parsing fix does not affect this behaviour at base.
The host/port parsing change is unrelated; a view returning a plain dictionary is still serialized to compact JSON with Content-Type application/json at head.
Missing required fields always raise a ValidationError in pydantic at both revisions; the generic alias schema-generation fix does not touch required-field validation.
Required-field validation is core pydantic behaviour unaffected by the generic-alias schema fix, so omitting the required field still raises a ValidationError at head.
logging.WARN and logging.WARNING are the same value (30), so the default sqlalchemy logger level blocks INFO SQL echo output with echo off and logs it with echo on at base, matching the expectation.
The WARN to WARNING rename is purely cosmetic since the constants are equal, so default-level suppression of SQL echo records behaves identically at head.

At base, once attribute methods are generated the method_missing fast path only checks the generated flag and delegates to attribute_missing, keeping aliased computed-attribute reads within a small multiple of real column reads.

At head method_missing now calls define_attribute_methods and rescues a NameError from public_instance_method on every access to the undefined computed attribute, adding large per-call overhead that pushes the ratio past 20x.
At base each dispatch adds a new WrappedListener to the callStack, so dispatching twice with one listener yields two entries from getCalledListeners, matching the expected invocation count.
At head postProcess deduplicates called listeners per event, so dispatching twice with one listener yields a single entry from getCalledListeners instead of the expected two invocations.
At base the generated bash completion script clears and sets COMPREPLY via direct assignment, so each subcommand's custom completion hook returns only its own scoped suggestions.

At head the shellcheck fix appends to COMPREPLY without resetting it, so completion entries computed earlier in handle_reply bleed into the custom hook's result and suggestions are no longer scoped to the active subcommand.
With qs 6.13.0 plain repeated keys are combined into an array regardless of count, so 25 repeated ids values parse as a 25-element array at base.
qs 6.14.0 applies the arrayLimit of 20 to implicitly repeated keys, so 25 ids values are converted into a plain object keyed by numeric index instead of an array at head.
At base get_environ_proxies takes only the url parameter, so calling it with a single URL argument succeeds and returns the proxy dictionary.
At head get_environ_proxies requires the new no_proxy parameter, so calling it with only a URL raises a TypeError instead of returning the proxy dict.
At base parse_unit_value rejects tokens starting with '.', so .foons is not treated as a duration and the list literal parses the bare word as the string '.foons'.

At head the parser accepts '.' as a unit-value start and .foons ends with the ns duration suffix, so it is parsed as an invalid duration/filesize instead of the string '.foons', producing a parser error.
At base a default temp sink and CURLOPT_FILE are always connected, so a HEAD request with an Accept-Encoding header completes normally through the cURL handler.
At head no sink is connected for HEAD requests, so with Accept-Encoding set cURL has nowhere to write decoded data and the request fails instead of returning a response.
At base the RHS map value falls through to Inspect in safe_to_algebra, and Inspect handles the improper list [1 | 2] fine, so the standard match-failure diff is reported without crashing.

At head the new escape/1 converts maps to AST via Map.to_list and build_map_or_struct before formatting, and the improper list value [1 | 2] crashes that conversion path while rendering the match-failure diff.
At base css_props registers a teardown that removes the element, so toggling the dynamic component destroys the node carrying the custom property and the red styling is lost.

At head the element-removal teardown is deleted and dynamic components share the corrected css_props/component ordering, so the custom property persists across the toggle with correct red styling and hydration.
At base the transform guard simply checks that the code contains 'new URL' and 'import.meta.url', so multi-line calls are still processed and the asset is emitted.

At head the new hook filter regex uses '.' without the s flag, so it fails to match when new URL and import.meta.url are split across lines and the multi-line reference is never transformed or emitted.
At base no environment variable carries the raw item text, so a NUL-containing item does not reach the child process environment and the preview command runs normally.
At head FZF_CURRENT_ITEM is built from the raw item text, and a NUL byte inside an environment string makes execve fail, so the preview child process cannot start and fzf reports the failure.
At base switching to edgeToEdge calls setSystemUiVisibility with only layout flags, which clears the HIDE_NAVIGATION and FULLSCREEN bits left by immersiveSticky so the system bars reappear.

At head the edgeToEdge branch returns after WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows(false) without clearing the immersive HIDE_NAVIGATION/FULLSCREEN visibility flags, so the bars stay hidden after the switch.
At base there is no multiple-assignment check for case patterns, so the valid ClassLabel(num_classes=num_classes) class pattern produces no syntax error.

At head the new visitor inserts the keyword attribute name into the binding set before visiting the keyword's capture pattern, so num_classes=num_classes is falsely flagged as a multiple assignment syntax error under preview.

At base decodeBodyToStruct indexes the destination slice without growing it, so decoding two blocks into a one-element value slice panics with an index out of range instead of overwriting the placeholder.

At head decodeBodyToStruct grows the destination slice with reflect.Append when the block index exceeds its length, so the two blocks decode into two entries without panic, overwriting the placeholder.
At base the mocked moment is only re-zoned when a timezone is explicitly given, so Carbon::now() without an argument keeps the America/Los_Angeles representation instead of the default UTC one.
At head the mock falls back to date_default_timezone_get() when no timezone is pinned, so reading now() without a timezone argument returns the reference moment in UTC as expected.
At base the protocol-relative regex requires two slashes followed by a non-slash character, so '///test.com' and '/<TAB>//test.com' are not classified as protocol-relative.
At head the expanded regex ([/\\]\s*){2,}[^/\\] matches three-plus leading slashes, whitespace between slashes, and mixed slashes, so all three inputs are classified protocol-relative.
Guava's md5 of the UTF-8 bytes of 'abc' has always produced 900150983cd24fb0d6963f7d28e17f72; the combineOrdered/Unordered accessor change does not affect hashing values.
The getBytesInternal refactor only avoids a defensive copy in hash combining and does not change MD5 outputs, so hashing 'abc' still yields the standard digest at head.
Moving the diagnostic descriptors into a dedicated class preserves codes, messages, and severities, so the source generator produces the same working client for a GET-annotated interface at base.
The pure diagnostic-refactor does not alter code generation, so the generated client still issues the expected GET request to the interface route at head.
Removing only redundant trailing continue statements does not change control flow, so a plain GET over HTTP/1.1 still returns the 200 body with matching Content-Length at base.
The needless_continue cleanup leaves dispatch and body-piping semantics identical, so the simple HTTP/1.1 fetch behaves the same at head.
At base to_iso8601/2 converts the date to the ISO calendar and then calls to_iso8601/1 without the format, so a :basic request on a Holocene date silently returns the extended '2001-01-01' form.
At head to_iso8601/2 forwards the requested format through the ISO-calendar conversion, so the Holocene date returns '2001-01-01' extended and '20010101' basic as expected.
On PHP 8.2+ the native end property is engine-managed at base; setEndDate updates internal state but leaves ->end showing the construction value 2024-09-30.
At head syncNativePeriod reinitializes the parent DatePeriod after setEndDate, so both the end property and getEndDate report 2025-06-15 00:00:00.
At base the headline builder has no whitespace validation, so the newline-containing path is transmitted in the request line instead of raising an invalid URI error.
At head the client checks the resolved request URI for whitespace and raises RequestError before sending, refusing the newline-embedded path as expected.
The Albanian pluralization change does not affect the default English locale, so 1000000 and 2000000 still humanize to 'one million' and 'two million' at base.
The Albanian locale data change does not touch the English number-to-words formatter, so 'one million' and 'two million' are still produced at head.
The property-loading fix does not affect scope resolution; a singleton declaration resolves to the same instance on both calls at base.
Filtering non-String property keys leaves singleton scoping untouched, so repeated resolutions return the identical instance at head.
replaceElement keeps the same append/swap/remove algorithm at base with a duplicate-key precondition, so replacing position 1 with 'z' preserves order and duplicate keys trap.
The shared _replaceNew primitive is behavior-preserving per the PR and identical steps, so key replacement, ordering, and duplicate-key errors work the same at head.
The manual negative clamp is equivalent to the built-in max refactor, so parsing '-5MB' clamps the negative byte count to 0 at base as expected.
max(cast.ToInt(sizeStr), 0) is exactly equivalent to the manual clamp, so the invalid '-5MB' value still parses to zero bytes at head.

At base findCaseInsensitivePathRec takes children[0] when wildChild is set, which is a static node here, and the unmatched /prefix/a/b/c path drives the node-type switch into a panic instead of a clean 404.

At head the recursive lookup tries static children via indices and takes the wildcard child from the end of the array, so mis-cased /PREFIX/XXX redirects to /prefix/xxx and unmatched paths return 404 without panicking.
At base toBigInt returns the nil Int when Exp is 0, so Int64Value dereferences it via IsInt64 and panics for a valid Numeric with no digits.
At head toBigInt returns big.NewInt(0) for a nil Int, so both Float64Value and Int64Value report zero with no runtime error.
The tab-stop rendering fix does not affect the event loop or quit signalling, so an external Quit still makes the program's Run return promptly at base.
The renderer tab-stop change does not alter event-loop shutdown, so calling Quit from another goroutine still makes Run return promptly at head.
At base RunUntilCancelledFuture polls the wrapped future before the cancellation check, so polling with an already-cancelled token starts the panicking inner operation.
At head run_until_cancelled checks is_cancelled first and returns None without ever polling the inner future, so the panicking operation never starts.
Skipping unreachable ignore files only changes traversal performance, not matcher semantics, so case-insensitive search still finds all case variants at base.
The ignore-file loading optimization leaves case-insensitive matching untouched, so every line containing the term is still reported at head.

The nesting refactor keeps identical logic (container has no default and the field skips deserialization implies Default::default()), so the skipped field still deserializes to its type default at base.
The flattening refactor is logically identical to the original nested condition, so a skipped field without custom defaults still receives Default::default() when absent from the input at head.
